faq.q: What are color harmonies and how do they work?
faq.a: Color harmonies are combinations of colors that are visually pleasing based on their relationships on the color wheel. Complementary colors are opposite each other, triadic uses three evenly spaced colors, analogous uses adjacent colors, and monochromatic uses variations of one color.

faq.q: How many colors should be in a design palette?
faq.a: Most effective color palettes contain 3-5 colors. This provides enough variety for visual interest while maintaining cohesion. Too few colors may be limiting, while too many can create visual chaos and reduce brand recognition.

faq.q: Can I check if my color palette is accessible?
faq.a: Yes, our color palette generator includes accessibility checking to ensure your color combinations meet WCAG guidelines for contrast ratios. This helps ensure your designs are readable for users with visual impairments.

faq.q: What export formats are available for color palettes?
faq.a: You can export color palettes as CSS variables, JSON data, Adobe Swatch Exchange (ASE) files, or simple text lists in HEX, RGB, or HSL formats. This makes it easy to use your palettes in any design software or development environment.

faq.q: What's the difference between complementary and analogous color schemes?
faq.a: Complementary colors are opposite on the color wheel (like red and green) creating high contrast and vibrant designs. Analogous colors are adjacent on the wheel (like blue, blue-green, green) creating harmonious, calming designs with less contrast.

faq.q: How do I create a professional brand color palette?
faq.a: Start with your primary brand color, then use our generator to create complementary or triadic harmonies. Include neutral colors for balance, ensure accessibility compliance, and test the palette across different media and backgrounds.
